newsitem.title: FRANCE: French mountain rescue chief injured in Norway.
newsitem.headline: French mountain rescue chief injured in Norway.

text.p: The chief of the prestigious French mountain rescue squad in the Mont Blanc range, Europe's highest, has been seriously hurt in a fall while training in Norway, the French army said on Friday.
A statement said Major Alain Esteve, 45, fell while climbing on a frozen waterfall near the Norwegian town of Hemsedal on Wednesday. He was in hospital in Oslo in serious condition.
Esteve has headed the army High Mountain Group (GHM) rescue service in the resort of Chamonix since 1986.
He climbed Mount Everest without oxygen in 1993 and walked to the North Pole last year.
He achieved the fastest-ever climb of Aconcagua, the Americas' highest mountain, in four and a half hours.
